tokenised-english.description: Reference text in which punctuation marks and clitics stand as separate tokens, as in the tagged English corpora of the Brown, LOB and Penn Treebank tradition ("It 's a pity , he said ."). The rules undo that layout on whichever string carries it, so that a transcription written with ordinary spacing is not charged for the reference's tokenisation. They change whitespace only: no other character is added, removed or replaced. In order: every run of whitespace becomes one space; double quotation marks (U+0022, U+201C, U+201D) standing at the edge of a word are detached from it on both strings, because the direction of a straight quotation mark cannot be decided within a line (they are never re-attached); the space before , . ; : ! ? is removed when the marks end a token, alone or followed only by closing brackets and further such marks; the space before a closing bracket and after an opening bracket is removed; the clitics 's 'll 're 'd 'm 've (any letter case, apostrophe U+0027 or U+2019) rejoin a preceding word; the Penn-style split negation n't rejoins a preceding word. The rules are applied until the text no longer changes. Single quotation marks are left as they are, because a detached one cannot be told from an apostrophe: on a comparison that counts spacing, a reference with detached single quotation marks is still charged to a system that attaches them. Typographic quotation marks are detached but not replaced by straight ones. Known limits: a quoted word equal to a clitic (he said 'Re: ...') is joined to the preceding word; spaced initialisms ("B B C") are not joined.
